Controllability: As indicated in Table 6, the HVAC system was run without dehumidification control during M&V operating periods (2)-(5), and the relative humidity at zone level always remains lower than 60% RH, which confirms that dehumidification was not necessary for the dry winter conditions. Note that the dewpoint setpoint is only activated in period (1) since the CRC control was not active during the other operating periods. As seen in Fig. 8, the supply air temperature closely follows the setpoint for the baseline cases (operating periods (3) and (5)), which are maintained nearly constant to ensure the required dewpoint is maintained. In operating modes (2) and (4), on the other hand, the HEDS controller adjusted the setpoint to approximately 80°F, which allows air to be recirculated without cooling to meet the zone temperatures. This logic reduces the cooling load on the chiller and the heating load on the reheat coils. 15 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. We note that there was a two-day period when the humidity in the North Gallery was significantly different from other zones, as seen in Fig. 9a, due to abnormal operation of Humidifier 1, which serves the North Gallery. Figure 9b shows that the control output of Humidifier 1 is close to 100% while output from Humidifier 2 is less than 60%. This is not expected to have a significant impact on the accuracy of M&V data since it is accounted for in the load calculations.
